sources.text: Can gravitational production from a hot Standard Model brane supply viable dark matter in the dark dimension, while relating its abundance to the dark-energy scale?

Numerically solves coupled Boltzmann equations for individual KK abundances, including brane production, decays back to Standard Model fields, and intratower daughter production. Early production also receives an analytic treatment using Bessel-function kernels.

Dimensional analysis of universal graviton–stress-tensor coupling estimates brane-to-bulk production. The expansion-compensated quantity y=ρKK/s gives production dominated by the initial temperature, conditional on approximate preservation of dark-sector mass.

What linear cosmological signatures arise from repeated decays within a dark-matter KK-graviton tower, and what do CMB, BAO and weak-lensing data imply for its kick velocity and Dark Dimension parameters?

Restrict weak lensing to estimated linear scales using k_NL^3 P_lin(k_NL,z)/(2π^2)=Δ_NL. Apply redshift-dependent multipole cuts, requiring cross-bin measurements to pass both cuts; compare Δ_NL=0.5 and 1.0.

Modify CLASS and sample v_today alongside six ΛCDM parameters with MontePython. Use Planck 2018 temperature, polarization and lensing, BAO, and KiDS-1000 band powers; sampling uses Metropolis–Hastings, with nested sampling for KiDS-only analyses.

Model the background momentum distribution with a moving Gaussian-like peak and fixed width parameter η=0.25. Use distribution moments and a fluid approximation truncating the Boltzmann hierarchy at multipole ℓ_max=2; shear terms are retained in the full analysis.

What bounds do CMB energy deposition, intergalactic heating, diffuse and Galactic photons, and Galactic positron production place on decaying KK-graviton dark matter and its coupling to the Standard Model brane?

Integrate energy injection over a continuous KK distribution, include delayed deposition through channel-dependent f-curves, and project deposition histories onto CMB principal components. The authors report agreement with ExoCLASS plus MontePython MCMC constraints.

Use modified DarkHistory evolution for ionization and IGM temperature. Galactic analyses integrate decay flux through a halo profile and compare binned INTEGRAL/NuSTAR observations; the 511 keV analysis instead limits total positron injection.

Compute redshift-integrated extragalactic photon flux including hydrogen photoionization attenuation. Use χ² likelihoods and Metropolis–Hastings sampling for conservative total-flux limits and stronger limits assuming astrophysics explains the measured background.
Can the radion of a micron-sized dark dimension be ultralight fuzzy dark matter, and can inflaton-fed KK graviton cascades supply its cosmological abundance?

The production estimate expands bulk fields into Fourier KK modes and sums graviton-to-radion-plus-lighter-graviton decay channels. The abundance estimate then uses a homogeneous scalar equation, a quadratic potential near its minimum, and radiation/matter redshifting.

Dimensional reduction of the five-dimensional Einstein–cosmological-constant action to the four-dimensional Einstein frame is used to identify the radion kinetic term and exponential potential. The authors relate compact-radius growth by N e-folds to noncompact Einstein-frame growth by 3N/2 e-folds.

Uses Gauss–Codazzi decomposition, background Einstein equations, Israel junction conditions and GHY boundary cancellations to obtain the graviton action. A Weyl transformation maps non-minimal scalar couplings to Einstein frame and absorbs their background effect into the warp factor.

Expands the action to cubic order, applies on-shell mode equations and integration by parts, and sums massive-spin-2 polarizations. Large-mode WKB overlaps and zeta-function channel sums supply the tower scaling estimates.

Does the KK-graviton three-point amplitude near threshold scale with the parent mass or daughter momentum, how general is the resulting cascade suppression, and what does it imply for cascading graviton dark matter?

Bound cascade overlaps using profile completeness, then sum daughter channels. For cosmology, sum decay photons over the freeze-in tower, include survival and redshift, and compare bin-integrated signals with archival Galactic and isotropic gamma-ray spectra.

Express the surviving three-graviton vertex as the square of a color-stripped Yang–Mills vertex. Use massive transverse-traceless polarization sums for the width and a parent-rest-frame partial-wave argument for its threshold behavior.

Expand the gravitational action to cubic order and integrate profile-gradient overlaps by parts using the mode equation. On shell, L_□ cancels L_m. The field redefinition h=e^H−1 gives an alternative explanation of their removal.

What is the near-threshold partial-wave suppression of intra-tower KK graviton decays, and does the resulting cascade rate permit dark-dimension graviton dark matter or evade bounds from unavoidable freeze-in production?

destinations.title: How is a KK-graviton population produced?
destinations.question: Can a hot Standard Model brane gravitationally produce the KK-graviton abundance needed in the Dark Dimension setting?
destinations.summary: The source studies initially unexcited bulk modes coupled to a hot Standard Model brane. Initial production and abundance are a distinct question from whether the produced population can subsequently cascade rapidly enough to remain viable dark matter.

excludes: late-time linear perturbation constraints as the primary target
regimes: Dark Dimension setup; source-specific cosmological assumptions

destinations.title: What controls the near-threshold cascade rate?
destinations.question: How does an intra-tower KK-graviton decay amplitude and rate scale with daughter momentum near threshold, and which background or coupling assumptions control that scaling?
destinations.summary: Two late-2026 sources in the frozen corpus argue for stronger threshold suppression than assumed in earlier rapid-cascade estimates. One studies cancellations and their scope in scalar–gravity systems; the other emphasizes the partial-wave interpretation and applies it to a flat dark dimension. Their contribution to this common question does not require treating their entire claims or regimes as equivalent.

excludes: unqualified universal statement for every field content or higher-derivative theory
automatic equivalence of all cosmological conclusions
assumptions: source-specific diffeomorphism-invariant couplings and background assumptions
regimes: near-threshold two-body decay; detailed paper-specific scope retained
conventions: Different momentum symbols must be identified in the parent rest frame before comparing threshold scalings.

destinations.title: What would repeated decays do to cosmological structure?
destinations.question: Within the specified repeated-decay KK-graviton model, how do daughter recoil and the changing mass distribution affect linear cosmological perturbations?
destinations.summary: The 2023 analysis propagates a simplified decay-driven population through linear cosmology and constrains a kick-velocity combination. Its observational calculation should be read together with the assumed cascade dynamics. The later threshold-rate question tests a premise of the rapid-cascade scenario; it is a separate connected destination.

excludes: new observational data beyond the frozen source
unconditional viability of the underlying cascade model
regimes: linear cosmological regime; dated source model and observations

destinations.title: What bounds survive if the cascade is suppressed?
destinations.question: In a flat dark dimension with threshold-suppressed KK-graviton cascades, what observational constraints follow from the irreducibly produced population even if it is not all dark matter?
destinations.summary: The 2026 source studies photon emission from an unavoidable freeze-in population and compares the resulting upper reheating bound with lower cosmological bounds. This asks a different question from fitting linear structure in the earlier fast-cascade model. The stated flat-dimension scope must remain visible.

excludes: all extra-dimensional models excluded without a scope argument
unqualified replacement of every earlier cosmological calculation
assumptions: near-threshold cascade suppression as argued in source
regimes: source-specific freeze-in/decay cosmology and observational assumptions
